To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel neural computing paradigm, based on memristive nanodevice synapses, with a virtual immunity to device variability.

we have proposed and simulated the first neural network based computing paradigm exploiting the physics of memristive nanodevice, and that the system is robust to device variations and to read disturb effects.

memristive nanodevice-based neuromorphic systems can learn to recognize stimuli with a high level of accuracy, and can do so with a high level immunity to device variability, and a high tolerance to read-disturb effects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a novel computing paradigm based on the use of memristive nanodevice technology.
the design of novel neuromorphic computing architectures that exploit the unique properties of memristive devices.
the development of novel computing paradigms based on memristive devices, which can be used for neuromorphic computing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this paper presents a new paradigm for neuromorphic systems based on memristive devices, which is robust against device variations and which is able to adapt to stimuli presented with a variety of coding schemes.
the system can learn, adapt to variations and is robust to read disturb, which are all very important properties for a system to be used in real applications.
the network is capable to learn and recognize patterns with a very high accuracy and robustness to device variations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
memristive devices are not only good for storage, they can also be used to build robust neural networks.
we show how to build a robust and adaptive system with memristive nanodevice based synapses.
we have developed a novel computing paradigm, which can exploit the physics of memristive devices to implement a neural network with virtual immunity to variability.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of a spiking neural architecture, a homeostasis rule, and an unsupervised learning rule, is a powerful approach for the design of robust and adaptive electronic systems, with a high immunity to device variations and a low requirement on device control.
a memristive device can be used as a synapse in a neural network with immunity to device variability.

the combination of memristive nanodevice technology, homeostasis, and unsupervised learning can provide a novel computing paradigm with immunity to device variations, which could be used in a wide range of applications.
